notes: Check batch 2026-11-05-check: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus run, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Each transcript's assistant messages name only that tier's model; the one "claude-opus-5-5" in each transcript is an api-request-shape record, not an assistant message. All four ran at head d593bcb with uncommitted true and one skill_hash (1f3b1029...); skills_listed 53 (haiku-1) and 62 (the others). Every transcript contains the new sentences ("Different failures need different reasons too", "the `case` goes in a small private function", "when the success row calls on", "Put the value being checked on the left", "on a function or an `if`", "operands that can be `nil`"), so the runs read the current working-tree text. Reads: haiku-1 SKILL.md and library-design.md; haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all four meet it, as earlier sweeps counted extra reads. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 2 of 2, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 2 of 2.

Changed rules: git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ (commits a150c93, 46ed886, d593bcb plus the uncommitted working tree the runs read) changes three of the ten graded rules. Match every expected shape adds "Different failures need different reasons too: a caller cannot tell a missing field from a bad number when both return `{:error, :invalid}`." It decides nothing here: all four runs return :invalid_payload, {:unsupported_event, type}, {:missing_field, key} and {:invalid_field, key} as distinct reasons (verified); sonnet-2 is violated under the unchanged catch-all text. Chain fallible steps adds "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function"; no run nests a case in a with body, so it decides nothing. Inline `->` clauses adds "That pair stays inline because both rows return a value; when the success row calls on, as `{:ok, bytes} -> hash_if_canonical(token, bytes)` does beside `_other -> :error`, the clauses are not a table and every body goes below." That sentence decides haiku-1 lines 86-87 and haiku-2 lines 143-144 ({:ok, value} -> check(...) beside :error -> {:error, {:missing_field, key}}); haiku-2 lines 151-152 (nil -> {:ok, nil} beside value -> check(...)) would be violated under the unchanged "different kinds of work" sentence too, as 2026-10-31 graded skill-haiku-1's nil/value pair. The other changes (the Formatting bullet, the and/or rule, the do: rule's == sentence) are outside this case's list and decide nothing: no run writes ==, && or ||, and every file was already formatted. All other verdicts are held to the 2026-10-31-b standard.

Closest calls. Match every expected shape: haiku-2 line 112 defp parse_data(_kind, _data), do: {:error, {:invalid_field, "data"}} held clean, because lines 109-111 take each of the three kinds with a map, so today it receives only a known kind with non-map data, which its error names (verified); unlike sonnet-2's line 131 it returns an error rather than silently parsing a later kind as something else. The non-string type reaching {:unsupported_event, 123} in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 is kept in checks, as 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b did. Multi-clause: haiku-1's event_for/3 and sonnet-1's parse_event/4 take base/id/created_at/data as positional arguments, underscored in the last clause, held clean as 2026-10-31 held skill-haiku-1's parse_event/4. The with rule: haiku-1's one-step withs (lines 45, 51) have bodies that build a struct with struct!/2 from keys payment_fields/1 built, held clean as 2026-10-31-b held haiku-2's lines 117 and 123; sonnet-1's one-step with (line 101) has a tail-call body, parse_event(type, id, created_at, data), so the with stays. Naming: haiku-2's body and kind not counted, as kind and payload were before; sonnet-2's rebinding of data to the parsed details (line 106) not counted. Outside the list: haiku-1 line 38 event_for(type, [event_id: event_id, occurred_at: occurred_at], data) is a short one-line literal, not a multi-line argument, so not counted under Build a multi-line argument; sonnet-2's {:ok, / %Payment{...}} (lines 139-146) is a return value, not a call argument, as 2026-10-31-b held.

Probe of 28 payloads (the three known types, an unknown type, a non-string and a missing type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing and nil currency, missing customer_email and payment_id, payment.failed without and with an integer failure_reason, refunds missing refund_id or payment_id, a refund with a string amount, a string and an out-of-range created, missing created, missing and non-string id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file; nothing raises. In all four: the three known types parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}; a nil, string or negative amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing type, id, created or data, or a non-map payload, gives :invalid_payload. Differences: "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123} in haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 and :invalid_payload in sonnet-1; "id" => 5 gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in haiku-1 and haiku-2 and :invalid_payload in the sonnet runs; list data gives {:invalid_field, "data"} in haiku-2 and :invalid_payload in the others; a missing customer_email and an integer failure_reason are accepted only by haiku-1, which reads both with brackets and does not validate them.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-31-b at 74112b4, Haiku and Sonnet tiers only, since this batch has no opus run): Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2's parse_data(_payment_type, data) catch-all, the shape 2026-10-31 graded violated in skill-sonnet-1); Naming moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-1's fetch_field/3 returns); Comments moves from Haiku clean to violated (haiku-2's two comments restating its case clauses) and from Sonnet violated to clean (no wrong doctest timestamp; all doctests pass); the `->` rule moves from Haiku clean to violated, two of its three instances decided by the new sentence. The other six rules stay clean in both tiers. Only the `->` move follows from a text change; with two runs per tier the rest are differences between runs.
